source.title: Langevin Dynamics with Continuous Tempering for High-dimensional Non-convex Optimization
source.authors: Nan-Yang Ye; Zhan-Xing Zhu; Rafał K. Mantiuk

record.file_problem: Full text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of a new optimizer on training and test performance in autoencoders and character-level language modeling, settings relevant to optimizer and generalization claims.
record.gate_note: Reports training and held-out results for CTLD and comparator optimizers. The reported outcomes bear on V4's optimizer/generalization comparison; the study does not test memorization capacity, width, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, batch size effects, dropout effects, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. The MNIST autoencoder result is given as learning curves without numerical values in the text.
record.test_reason: The reported held-out comparison evaluates CTLD against other optimizers. It does not report SGD's held-out performance: SGD-M is omitted from Figure 3, and Appendix E.2 reports only its training perplexity. CTLD's superiority over Adam and RMSProp therefore does not establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD generalization comparison. The remaining experiments do not measure any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but narrower than the conclusion: the authors argue that continuous-tempering Bayesian sampling improves exploration before optimization and claim CTLD's superiority over existing methods. They report the best training and test perplexities in the character-language-model experiment.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces continuous-tempering Langevin sampling followed by stochastic optimization, compared with the optimizer methods in V4; evaluates language modeling and stacked denoising autoencoders rather than the listed V4 benchmark mix.
record.method_sensitivity: CTLD's sensitivity analysis reports a slight, limited improvement with a larger temperature range parameter S; the result concerns CTLD's held-out perplexity, not the optimizer comparison itself.

fits_no_version.finding: CTLD achieves the best training and test perplexities among the plotted character-language-model optimizers; Adam and RMSProp converge quickly initially. SGD-M is absent from those plots, with only training perplexity above 3.1 reported separately.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continuous-tempering sampling followed by momentum SGD can improve character-language-model optimization and held-out performance over the tested comparator recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: CTLD is initially slower during autoencoder sampling but reportedly reaches the best final reconstruction results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continuous-tempering initialization can improve final autoencoder training reconstruction loss.

record.code_released: https://github.com/karpathy/char-rnn (referenced for initialization methods and model parameters; no CTLD code URL stated)
record.problems: Optimizer outcomes for the character-level language model are shown in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The MNIST autoencoder discussion gives no numeric held-out metric. No control comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted under the 60-row limit. Figure-only comparator outcomes are included because the text reports the comparison, but their individual numeric perplexities cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Held-out error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization and local connectivity.
Held-out adaptive-versus-SGD performance under limited or broader tuning; weight-decay and Adam-to-SGD remedies. SGD's training difficulty alone cannot establish the held-out comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout effects on held-out error; dropout is held fixed in the autoencoder experiment.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures. Flat-minimum arguments motivate CTLD but are not tested.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed V4 limits_scope verdict: unavailable SGD test results are an untested comparison, not evidence that V4 needs qualifying. CTLD sensitivity results and computation-time comparisons do not test any version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error versus network width beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Image classification comparisons and broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: CTLD

conditions.value: rate of 0.2 except for the first and last layer

rows.measure: Mean square error learning curves; final-stage held-out metric not stated.
rows.note: The text says CTLD was not as fast as other methods in the sampling phase and could fine-tune to the best final results, but no numeric test error is stated.
rows.check: Training reconstruction MSE for the proposed method, without a held-out measure; this does not test V4. CTLD is an optimizer, not a model.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Wikipedia Hutter Prize 100MB character-level LSTM, 20 epochs
reader_labels.reason: CTLD is reported to achieve the best training and test perplexities, but this comparison does not establish that adaptive optimizers generally underperform SGD; the plotted comparator values are not numerically stated (R2–R7). The study also reports that the SdA sampling phase was slower than other methods, though it is not a test-error result (R1).
